# Declared CLI option graph: every command path with its arguments, flags, help text,
# argument parsers, conflicts, defaults and required/hidden state.
#
# Shared field tables (packages/cli/src/commands/field-options.ts) feed several verbs and
# families from one spec, and the argv-mapping tests only observe flags an argv actually
# uses. This fixture is the detector for a flag that is dropped, renamed, reworded, or has
# its parser, conflict or default silently changed.
#
# Regenerate after an intentional change:
#   UPDATE_OPTION_GRAPH=1 npx vitest run packages/cli/tests/option-graph.test.ts
# then review the diff as a user-visible help change.

command (root)
  aliases=[]
  summary=
  opt --version | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Print the CLI version and exit
  opt --daemon-url <url> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Daemon WebSocket URL
  opt --json | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=false | help=Print raw protocol responses as JSON
  opt --dry-run | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=false | help=Preview a mutation without persisting it (validates, resolves the target, runs all guards). Ignored for read commands.
  opt --timeout-ms <ms> | parser=parsePositiveInt | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Client wait for the daemon response, in ms (default 60000). Distinct from bridge serve --request-timeout-ms.

command world search
  aliases=[]
  summary=Search world (and optionally compendium) documents through the bridge index
  opt --query <query> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=Search query (2-256 characters; terms are AND-combined)
  opt --mode <mode> | parser=<anonymous> | conflicts=[] | choices=["name","full"] | required=false | hidden=false | default="name" | help=Fields to search: "name" (stored names only) or "full" (names + body text + the Actor/Item system walk, with snippets)
  opt --types <list> | parser=parseSearchTypeList | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Comma-separated document types to search: Actor,Item,ActiveEffect,JournalEntry,JournalEntryPage,JournalEntryCategory,Scene,Token,Region,RegionBehavior,Macro,Playlist,PlaylistSound,RollTable,TableResult,Cards,Card,Folder (default: all)
  opt --include-compendia | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Also search compendium pack entry NAMES (off by default)
  opt --source <source> | parser=<anonymous> | conflicts=[] | choices=["world","pack"] | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Return only one section: "world", or "pack" (which requires --include-compendia)
  opt --limit <n> | parser=parsePositiveInt | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Maximum number of entries to return
  opt --offset <n> | parser=parseNonNegativeInt | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Number of entries to skip before this page

command cards deal
  aliases=[]
  summary=Deal cards FROM --cards-id TO each --to stack (each receives --count). Requires --idempotency-key: a retry deals ANOTHER batch. NEVER use this to give dealt cards BACK: `deal` has no return-to-origin branch, so dealing a card into a stack that already holds its id DESTROYS it (Foundry rejects the destination's create while the source-side delete in the same batch lands) — use `cards pass --card-ids` or `cards draw` from the origin stack instead. An UNAVOIDABLE collision is refused with INVALID_PARAMS; an avoidable one is left to Foundry.
  opt --cards-id <cardsId> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=SOURCE card stack id (the stack dealt FROM)
  opt --idempotency-key <key> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=REQUIRED: client-supplied key so a retried move returns the original result instead of moving ANOTHER batch of cards. Reuse the SAME key across retries of one move.
  opt --to <list> | parser=parseIdList | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=Comma-separated DESTINATION card stack ids
  opt --count <count> | parser=parsePositiveInt | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Cards per destination (integer >= 1)
  opt --how <how> | parser=<anonymous> | conflicts=[] | choices=["top","bottom","random"] | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Which cards to take: top (Foundry's FIRST/TOP=0), bottom (LAST/BOTTOM=1) or random (2)
  opt --no-chat | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Suppress Foundry's chat notification

command combat roll-initiative
  aliases=[]
  summary=Roll initiative through Foundry's own Combat#rollInitiative / rollAll / rollNPC
  opt --combat-id <combatId> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=Combat id
  opt --idempotency-key <key> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=true | hidden=false | default=- | help=REQUIRED: client-supplied key so a retried roll returns the original result instead of re-rolling and posting more chat. Reuse the SAME key across retries of one roll.
  opt --combatant-ids <ids> | parser=parseIdList | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Comma-separated combatant ids to roll (exact: an unknown or unowned id is REFUSED, because Foundry would silently skip it; a REPEATED id is refused too, because Foundry rolls and announces once per entry while the row stores one initiative)
  opt --all | parser=- | conflicts=["combatantIds","npc"] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Roll every combatant that has no initiative yet (Combat#rollAll)
  opt --npc | parser=- | conflicts=["combatantIds"] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Roll every NPC combatant that has no initiative yet (Combat#rollNPC)
  opt --formula <formula> | parser=- | conflicts=[] | choices=- | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Initiative formula override, evaluated by Foundry's own dice parser. THE GAME SYSTEM MAY IGNORE IT: core honours it, but dnd5e drops it for any combatant that HAS an actor (the normal case) and rolls that actor's own initiative instead. `rolled[].initiative` is read from stored state, so check it against the formula you asked for.
  opt --roll-mode <mode> | parser=<anonymous> | conflicts=[] | choices=["public","gm","blind","self"] | required=false | hidden=false | default=- | help=Chat visibility of the initiative messages (translated per Foundry version; default public). An EXPLICIT mode OVERRIDES Foundry's hidden-combatant privacy default, so `--roll-mode public` PUBLICLY reveals a hidden combatant's initiative.
